title: Parity: env var + CLI flag to relocate the sigstore and blob-info cache dirs
body:
Rootless podman writes two things under `$HOME/.local/share/containers` that sit outside `storage.conf`'s reach (different subsystem — containers/image):

1. Signature cache: `$HOME/.local/share/containers/sigstore` for unprivileged users (default documented in `containers/registries.d.5`). Observed live: blocking that path makes every pull fail at the "reading signatures" stage with `ENOTDIR`.
2. Blob-info cache (`pkg/blobinfocache`, sqlite backend; default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/containers/cache`, falling back to `~/.local/share/containers/cache`).

Source-checked, not just a help-text skim:
- Sigstore default (`containers/image` `docker/registries_d.go`): `defaultUserDockerDir = ".local/share/containers/sigstore"`, joined onto legacy `$HOME` via `filepath.Join(homedir.Get(), ...)` in `builtinDefaultLookasideStorageDir` — `XDG_DATA_HOME` is not consulted. No env var and no podman flag addresses it.
- Blob cache (`containers/image` `pkg/blobinfocache/default.go`): honors `XDG_DATA_HOME`, degrades to a memory-only cache on any failure (never fatal). The library field `SystemContext.BlobInfoCacheDir` exists and buildah exposes it as a (hidden) `--blob-info-cache-dir` flag — but podman hardcodes it to empty (`pkg/domain/infra/abi/artifact.go`) and exposes no flag (checked `podman --help` and `podman build --help`).

Use case: users who must keep that tree empty or redirected (sealed or redirected home directories; in my case a mode-0000 tripwire file that turns silent store repopulation into a loud failure instead of mystery state). Today the sigstore half breaks every pull with no recourse.

Notes: `registries.d` `lookaside` / `lookaside-staging` relocates signature *storage* per registry — related but not a global directory override, undiscoverable for this purpose, and it does not cover the blob cache.

Sibling parity status (what is already first-class, for calibration):

| Path | Env | CLI flag |
|---|---|---|
| graphroot / runroot / driver opts | `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` (the conf file itself is env-only) | `--root` / `--runroot` / `--storage-driver` / `--storage-opt`, `TMPDIR` / `--tmpdir` |
| registry auth | `REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE` | `--authfile` |
| registries.d location | — (`SystemContext.RegistriesDirPath` exists) | skopeo: `--registries.d`; podman: none |
| blob-info cache | `XDG_DATA_HOME` (generic default, honored) | none in podman (buildah: hidden `--blob-info-cache-dir`) |
| sigstore default | none — ignores `XDG_DATA_HOME` entirely | none |

The sigstore default is the only path with neither env, flag, XDG support, nor global config override (same `$HOME`-join pattern as the per-user registries.d itself); the blob cache has XDG but no dedicated knob.

Ask: env + CLI-flag parity in podman for both defaults (names up to maintainers), or documented XDG support for the sigstore default.

comments.body: Please follow our proper issue templates and see https://github.com/podman-container-tools/community/blob/main/LLM_POLICY.md

Really, my first thought is … why?! User home directories exist … for a reason; if _anything_ can be assumed to be writable by an unprivileged user, certainly the home directory is the only location that can be assumed to be writable.

So, if pulls need to maintain mutable state for the blob info cache, well, that implies that the pull process must run with a mutable home directory.

---

> Use case: users who must keep that tree empty

No human user would want a home directory like that, and for specialized tools … well, it’s still the case that pulls need a location to store mutable state, and I don’t know why that should be a special tunable and not the tool’s $HOME.

> or redirected

I don’t know what the exercise of removing mutable state from $HOME and moving it into some other directory achieves. Assuming there is the pull process, and _some other_ process running under that UID, and the two don’t mutually trust each other (otherwise worrying about $HOME would be unnecessary): as long as the two processes run under the same kernel UID, and the mutable path is _resolvable_ as an absolute path (an ~implementation restriction, almost certainly), what security property is achieved by not making the mutable path stored in $HOME, but in some other environment variable / configuration? The other process, if it were malicious, can still find the path out and can still write files there.

(It is an interesting thought experiment to have a truly capability-based file system, where individual processes are not given $HOME and permissions to access ~all of it, but capabilities to their individual config/state spaces, and capabilities that correspond to the CLI arguments. But that’s not today’s Linux at all.)

Ultimately, for containment, it is possible to use separate UIDs, or containers.

---

In practice, I’d expect the default lookaside location (`.local/share/containers/sigstore`) to ~just work, even read-only (it cleanly fails on `ENOENT`) unless users _specifically_ break it by creating a 000 parent directory or something similar at the expected path. And the blob info cache can be redirected using $XDG_DATA_HOME — even granting the assumption that the process is not allowed to write to $HOME at all, $XDG_DATA_HOME should be redirected in any case, so I think that’s sufficient.

Ultimately, for containment, it is possible to use separate UIDs, or containers.

I don’t think it makes much sense to keep adding CLI options for every single path the binary might want to use: It’s a hassle to develop and maintain, _and_ a hassle to use, all for … some experiment in designing a system incompatible with the way ordinary Linux is used? While I appreciate such experiments, and they can grow to something very valuable, I don’t think Podman should be paying the cost for them in advance. (A lot of the CLI options that exist to redirect paths were added only for purposes of our integration tests, and if I had my way, we would never have these options in the primary binaries; instead we would build a test-only binary that adds these options.)
